newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra sees Telstra vote soon - Alston.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra sees Telstra vote soon - Alston.

text.p: Australian communications minister Richard Alston said he expected parliament's upper house to vote in the near future on legislation aimed at selling part of state telecommunications giant Telstra Corp.
"It (the legislation) will come back in fairly soon," Alston told Perth radio station 6PR.

The government does not have a majority in the upper house, the Senate, and needs the support of at least two non-government senators to have the Telstra legislation passed. The Labor opposition and minor parties have pledged to block the sale, but two independent senators have not yet declared their position.
The Liberal-National government wants to sell one-third of Telstra in its first term of office, raising about A$8 billion.
Both houses of parliament resume on Tuesday for a two-week sitting. Debate on the Telstra legislation is expected to resume later this month.
The sell-off legislation returns to the lower house for reconsideration if the Senate rejects or amends it.

Under Australia's constitution, the government can call an early election, followed by a joint sitting of both houses of parliament, if the Senate rejects legislation twice within six months. -- Canberrra bureau 61-6 273-2730
